definition: Quotidian means occurring every day and unremarkable for that reason.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word quotidian. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know quotidian should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Retirement, he warned us, strips the quotidian scaffolding from a day — no train to catch, no desk to reach by nine.
Routine is the milder marker — a routine check is simply the standard one; quotidian folds the task into the very texture of every day.
Humdrum goes further than quotidian: quotidian says a thing belongs to every day, while humdrum adds that the sameness has gone dull and gray.

Everyday is the plain-register twin of quotidian: both mark what a person meets daily. But everyday simply labels the category and passes no judgment on the sameness, while quotidian invites you to notice dailiness itself — in a seminar or a poem, often with respect.

Workaday describes what is built for plain, practical use — workaday boots, workaday prose that gets the job done. Quotidian is about recurrence instead: a thing is quotidian because it happens every day, whether or not it is practical, and the word can carry real respect.

For one year, the photographer Ana Reyes shot a single frame every morning: her kitchen table, seven o'clock, whatever happened to be on it.
Critics who expected drama were puzzled.
The images are quotidian by design -- a folded newspaper, a jar of pencils, toast.
Seen one at a time, they are almost nothing.
Seen as a wall of 365 prints, they become a calendar of a life.
Pill bottles arrive in March and multiply.
The newspaper stops coming in June.
Reyes says the project taught her that the repeated day is not the enemy of meaning but its container -- you only see a life change by watching what it does every morning.
